capabilities.name: access control and authentication
capabilities.limits: local accounts, scrypt, signed expiring tokens, roles; no external identity provider, no multi-factor authentication, no device binding

capabilities.name: consent records and purposes
capabilities.limits: append-only hash-chained log; a consent is a record of what the subject agreed, not a legal instrument; its validity under the applicable law is not assessed

capabilities.name: deletion requests and verification of the result
capabilities.limits: crypto-shredding plus removal of blobs and identity; copies outside the vault (backups, snapshots, journalling file systems) are not known unless listed

capabilities.name: encryption at rest
capabilities.limits: stdlib encrypt-then-MAC construction, not a vetted AEAD; passphrase-derived master key in process memory; no hardware key protection

capabilities.name: integrity of the originals
capabilities.limits: digests and authenticated encryption detect a change; they do not say the original was measured

capabilities.name: signatures or trusted checkpoints
capabilities.limits: Lamport one-time signatures chained from a trust anchor; the anchor must be published where the vault's holder cannot change it (not done here); key custody is not solved

capabilities.name: separation of identity from observation data
capabilities.limits: separation by pseudonym and by file; a pseudonym plus outside knowledge can still identify (re-identification from the data themselves is not assessed)

capabilities.name: no sensitive data in logs
capabilities.limits: identifiers and codes only in the audit log; redaction is a safety net; logs of other components (web server, proxies) are outside this layer

threats.threat: reading data or identities without authority
threats.defence: token required for every operation; a permission per operation; identities readable by the steward role only; every read audited

threats.threat: writing data without authority or without consent
threats.defence: data.write permission, an active consent for the purpose and data class, record validation before storage

threats.threat: tampering with stored records, skeletons or the class of a record
threats.defence: authenticated encryption (a tampered blob does not decrypt), record digests, a hash-chained ledger, integrity verification

threats.threat: forging, replaying or extending a token
threats.defence: HMAC-signed payload, expiry, revocation, constant-time comparison
scrypt hashes, a minimum length, lockout after repeated failures, equal work for unknown users

threats.threat: linking observation data to a person through the stores
threats.defence: identity kept only in an encrypted separate store; every other store carries the pseudonym only

threats.threat: sensitive information leaking through logs and error messages
threats.defence: the audit log and the errors carry identifiers and codes only; redaction of messages; tested with planted canaries

threats.threat: data remaining after a deletion request
threats.defence: blob removal with overwrite, destruction of the subject's wrapped key, removal of the identity, tombstone, verification with residual risks stated

threats.threat: use of data beyond the consented purpose, after revocation or expiry
threats.defence: the purpose and data class are checked against the consent log at the time of each use

threats.threat: rewriting the history (ledger, audit) without detection
threats.defence: hash chains, and signed checkpoints that commit to the heads (verified against a published anchor)

threats.threat: opening the vault without the passphrase
threats.defence: the master key is derived from the passphrase with scrypt; a check value rejects a wrong one; the key is not stored
